clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text (44 FR 1067) states no end for section 1-101, read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog. The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints the order as a note under 5 U.S.C. 5948 with no ending statement; 5 U.S.C. 5948 is in force and its 2000 amendments removed the fixed-date limit on agreements; 5 CFR part 595 (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) cites E.O. 12109 in its authority line; no held later instrument amends or revokes the designation. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 1-101 designates and empowers the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for physicians' comparability allowances. It has no own-terms end and no held instrument ends or amends it; 5 U.S.C. 5948 remains in force and 5 CFR part 595 relies on the order, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 1-102 says that until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979), pursuant to Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission shall exercise the authority delegated under the order. The condition occurred on January 1, 1979: the held text of Executive Order 12107, section 1-101, makes the establishment of the Office of Personnel Management under the Reorganization Plan effective on that date, and section 1-102's own wording sets that date as the latest. The actor is the order itself (own terms); the first end is the date the Office of Personnel Management was established, January 1, 1979, so the Civil Service Commission's exercise ended then. The inclusive reading (the clause runs through the end of December 31, 1978) and the alternative reading (the clause ends when January 1, 1979 begins) coincide in practice because the condition is the establishment of a body on that day.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12109 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1067; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12109.txt, read in full) has two numbered sections. Section 1-101 designates the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for payment of comparability allowances to recruit and retain certain Federal physicians. Section 1-102 provides that, until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979) under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission exercises that authority. The packet inventory already separates the two sections, so no inventory correction was needed. Section 1-102 ended by its own terms when the Office of Personnel Management was established: the held text of Executive Order 12107 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12107.txt), section 1-101, provides that the establishment of the Office of Personnel Management under sections 101 and 103 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 is effective on January 1, 1979. Executive Order 12107 does not amend Executive Order 12109 and is cited only for that date. Section 1-101 has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. current-law:usc has 1 hit, the U.S. Code note that prints this order under 5 U.S.C. 5948, with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 1 hit, 5 CFR part 595 (Physicians' Comparability Allowances), whose authority line cites E.O. 12109, 44 FR 1067, Jan. 3, 1979 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-part595.txt). later-events:ofr_catalog has 0 hits and the Office of the Federal Register catalog record carries no disposition note. A search of the held texts for the number 12109 finds only the order's own copies, the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12109.txt, which records no later instrument) and 5 CFR part 595; none amends, revokes or supersedes the order. The authority statute 5 U.S.C. 5948 (held text jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s5948.txt) is in force: its 2000 amendments (Pub. L. 106-571, section 2(a)(1)) struck the earlier sentence that barred agreements after a fixed date, and subsection (a) still refers to regulations that the President or his designee may prescribe. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.

savings.reason: Section 1-102 ended on January 1, 1979 when the Office of Personnel Management was established; it was a transitional allocation of the same delegated authority to the Civil Service Commission, and no action under it needs saving beyond what the continuing delegation in 1-101 and 5 CFR part 595 already govern. No claim is made that any residual duty under 1-102 survives.
